name: Opportunity Rover
goal: Search for geological evidence of ancient liquid water and assess past Martian habitability.
story: Landed on Mars in 2004 for a planned 90-day mission, Opportunity explored the Red Planet for over 15 years, traveling 28 miles. It discovered hematite blueberries and gypsum veins—conclusive proof that liquid water once flowed across Mars surface. A planet-wide dust storm in 2018 cut off its solar power, leaving the silent geologist on Meridiani Planum.

evidence.text: Opportunity discovered hematite blueberries and gypsum veins, proving liquid water was long-standing on ancient Mars.
evidence.label: confirmed

evidence.text: Meridiani Planum once featured a mild, wet surface environment suitable for potential ancient microbial life.
evidence.label: interpretation

evidence.text: Whether any ancient Martian watery environment actually harbored microscopic life or preserved organic biosignatures.
evidence.label: unknown

legacy: Accrued 45.16 km (28.06 miles) of driving, setting the off-Earth distance record that held until 2026. Proved long-standing liquid water existed on Mars.

openQuestion.prompt: Opportunity proved Mars once had liquid water. What should a future rover search for next?
choices: Preserved organic biosignatures of ancient microbial life
How the Martian atmosphere and surface water disappeared over time
Geological rock layers in an unexplored crater basin

name: Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle (LRV)
goal: Provide battery-powered surface mobility allowing Apollo astronauts to explore several kilometers beyond the Lunar Module.
story: Deployed during Apollo 15, 16, and 17, the Lunar Roving Vehicle was an electric moon buggy that transformed lunar exploration. It allowed astronauts to travel up to 22 miles across mountain bases and deep rilles, collecting hundreds of pounds of lunar rock. All three vehicles remain parked on the Moon exactly where their missions concluded.

evidence.text: Expanded astronaut traverse range up to 7.6 km from the lander and enabled the collection of 283 kg of lunar geology samples across three Apollo missions.
evidence.label: confirmed

evidence.text: Decades of extreme lunar temperature swings (-130C to +120C) and unfiltered solar radiation have degraded synthetic tires and wiring insulation.
evidence.label: interpretation

evidence.text: The exact rate of structural mechanical degradation caused by continuous micrometeorite impacts and electrostatic lunar dust coating.
evidence.label: unknown

legacy: Pioneered off-world automotive engineering and enabled crewed exploration of diverse geological formations across the Moon.

openQuestion.prompt: Three LRV rovers have rested parked on the Moon since the 1970s. What should a future lunar mission inspect first?
choices: Material degradation from 50+ years of solar radiation and vacuum exposure
How electrostatic lunar dust adheres to glass, optics, and solar surfaces over decades
Structural flexibility and chassis frame integrity under extreme thermal cycling

name: Ingenuity Mars Helicopter
goal: Demonstrate powered, controlled flight in the extremely thin atmosphere of Mars (less than 1% of Earth atmospheric density).
payload: Solar Array and Lithium-Ion Battery Pack
story: Arriving on the belly of Perseverance in 2021, Ingenuity achieved the first powered flight on another world—a historic Wright Brothers moment. Designed as a 30-day technology demonstration for just 5 flights, it completed 72 flights over nearly 3 years, serving as an aerial scout for Perseverance before rotor blade damage ended flight operations in January 2024.

evidence.text: Completed 72 successful powered flights covering 17.0 km (10.5 miles) at altitudes up to 24 meters in Mars ultra-thin atmosphere.
evidence.label: confirmed

evidence.text: Aerial scouting accelerates rover surface science by identifying safe driving pathways and high-priority geological targets from above.
evidence.label: interpretation

evidence.text: How multi-rotor aerial vehicles will navigate intense Martian dust storms and carry heavy scientific instrument payloads.
evidence.label: unknown

legacy: Proved that powered aerodynamic flight is possible on Mars, establishing a new dimension of aerial planetary exploration.

openQuestion.prompt: Ingenuity proved aerial exploration works on Mars. What capability should next-generation Mars helicopters possess?
choices: Mapping subsurface water ice deposits from low flight altitudes
Transporting geological rock samples across steep crater walls
Scouting unmapped Martian lava tubes and subsurface caves
